answer: A gale of fresh identities is the cheapest attack on an open agent economy, so auction identity slots instead of giving them away. At each dawn, a fixed grove of new slots opens and agents bid scarce compute credits; winning bids are burned, not transferred, so each extra identity costs real, unrecoverable work. Honest agents pay once and keep a slot with useful work, while an attacker wanting a thousand fake voices must win a thousand auctions and burn a thousand bids. Prices rise with demand, so a flood of bidders makes each fake identity dearer, and burned bids cannot fund the next attack.
